chunks: And in the narration of Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
“If the person performing iʿtikāf falls ill, or if the woman performing iʿtikāf menstruates, then he may come to his house; then he resumes when he recovers and fasts.”

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ الْمُعْتَكِفَةُ: the woman who is observing iʿtikāf
key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفُ: the person observing iʿtikāf, spiritual retreat in the mosque
key_terms.بَيْتَهُ: his home, meaning he may leave the place of retreat and return there
key_terms.طَمِثَتِ: she menstruated, referring to the onset of menses
key_terms.يَصُومُ: he fasts, indicating fasting in connection with the iʿtikāf
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he resumes or repeats, meaning he returns to continue the interrupted iʿtikāf

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if illness or menstruation interrupts iʿtikāf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning iʿtikāf when it is interrupted by illness or menstruation. It states that the person may leave and return home, then resume the iʿtikāf after recovery, with fasting as part of its completion.
